title: Waiting hours at the Veterans' Hospital
summary: After Dr. Murphy suggested the Veterans' Hospital, Marge got Zutty there by cab in snow and ice and they waited from 2:30 to 8 pm; the neurologist found a clot on the left side, a slight stroke.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well Zutty, when you, now another thing is from the way you tell it, the effect of the stroke was not, what happened after you felt this, you know, did......
Well it wasn't a massive stroke.
Well it couldn't have been.
Because I called Doctor Murphy.
And Marge explained it to him.

And Doctor Murphy said it sounds like a stroke. And so he said, I'm going to call the Veteran's Hospital and you take him down. And he called me back, said I'll call you back. Said you have Zutty down there around one o'clock, don't rush.

And when we went down there they had a bed for Zutty and all. We had to sit in that Veteran's Hospital from about 2.30 until 8 o'clock at night. The Neurologist wasn't there. Until 8 o'clock at night and Zutty was getting worse and worse. And they had some crazy guys you know out of the army, young fellows who were there to be admitted. And one got in a wheel chair and was running all around the place. And the other one was talking crazy. We had to sit through all of that.
And I'd go up, I admitted Zutty. I had Zutty to sit down but God had his arms around us because when
we left that hotel he said I can't get an ambulance. Because Zutty said, you'll have to bring him down in a cab.
Well how, how bad were you?
He was dragging the one side.
Oh I see, but you could walk?
Yes, but he could walk, he could walk. We got out of the hotel........
We were going to take a cab.

Yes, but a guy from the union, one of those guys that hung around the union, a colored guy that you knew so well he helped you into the and took a cab. Just luckily he was coming along and he helped you in the cab. Because there was a lot of high snow and ice there. And he helped Zutty into the cab. We got out of the cab at the Veteran's and I held on to Zutty and Zutty dragged into the Veteran's Hospital. And I sat Zutty down, I told him, I'll do all the paper work you know, the admittance and all.
Well how long were you in the hospital?
He didn't stay. After we sat there waiting until 8 o'clock and when the neurologist

did show up, I hadn't had a bit to eat or drink from 2.30 until 8 o'clock at night. And then the neurologist told Zutty that he had a clot on this side, on the left side. But said, when you have a stroke, if you have a clot of one side it affects the opposite side.
Yes.

See, and that's why he had this slight stroke not massive. He had this small blood clot on this side. And he gave Zutty an examination and he said, yes, it's a stroke and sort of sclerosis you know, all the medical terms and all.
